text.p: Australia's total commodity export performance is forecast to strengthen to a growth rate of 7.3 percent in 1997/98, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its March quarter Australian Commodities bulletin.

The slightly accelerated commodities export growth which ABARE sees for the coming financial year is based on an expected return to growth in some farm exports, particularly beef and wool, and on gains in some mineral exports, particularly gold, aluminium, alumina and nickel. Iron ore and coal exports were also seen growing.

ABARE's March quarter Commodities bulletin, released on Tuesday, forecast the total value of Australian commodity exports in 1997/98 to rise by 7.3 percent to A$62.43 billion compared with the 7.0 percent 1997/98 growth it forecast in February.
Total growth in Australia's commodites exports in 1996/97 was forecast at 1.3 percent, taking the overall export figure to A$58.20 billion.
The forecast percentage gain is slightly less than the 1.8 percent rise forecast in February and slightly less again than the 2.5 percent forecast in ABARE's December quarter papers.
ABARE's latest forecast has Australian farm exports rising by 2.8 percent to A$20.97 billion in 1997/98, up on the February forecast of zero gain to A$20.19 billion.
In 1996/97, farm exports are now forecast to be down by 0.4 percent to A$20.40 billion, against the 1.1 percent decline to A$20.19 billion forecast in January.
In 1996/97, a significant increase in the value of dairy products is expected to partly offset declines in the values of wheat and beef exports, ABARE said in its latest forecast.
In 1997/98, the value of beef exports is forecast to grow strongly, while wool exports are forecast to rise and dairy exports to continue to grow.
Exports of mineral resource commodities in 1997/98 are forecast to rise by 9.9 percent to A$39.

Farm unit export returns are forecast to rise by 1.1 percent in 1997/98 after a 13.4 percent fall in 1996/97, a slightly less optimistic forecast than a 2.0 percent gain for 1997/98 and a 14.0 percent fall for 1996/97 forecast in February.
ABARE's forecasts are based on an assumed strengthening of economic growth in response to lower domestic interest rates.
Forecast 1996/97 economic growth of 3.2 percent and 3.7 percent in 1997/98 are steady with the February forecast.
Headline inflation is assumed to average about 1.6 percent in 1996/97, before increasing to 2.0 percent in 1997/98.
The Australian dollar is assumed to average about 78 U.S. cents in 1997/98, steady with 1996/97.
